title: ASSERTION 2: God known by natural mental discourse, but most imperfectly
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): SECOND ASSERTION. God by ye natural discourse belonging toward our mind is indeed known, but in a most imperfect way. Since by sense God cannot be perceived, whether by reason we can perceive Him we inquire. But much more faintly God from His effects we know, which by God infinitely are surpassed. Hence Nazianzen correcting Plato: God's nature by no words can be explained, plus by mind plus intellect still less comprehended.
pass_b_english: SECOND ASSERTION. God is indeed known by the natural discourse of our mind, but in a most imperfect way.

Since God cannot be perceived by sense, we inquire whether we can perceive Him by reason. But we know God much more faintly from His effects, which are infinitely surpassed by God. Hence Nazianzen, correcting Plato: God's nature can be explained by no words, and by mind and intellect can be comprehended still less.
source_text: ASSERTIO SECUNDA. Deus naturali mentis nostrae discursu cognoscitur quidem, sed imperfectissimo modo. Cum sensu percipi non possit Deus, an ratione eum percipere possimus inquiremus. Multo languidius Deum cognoscimus ex effectis suis, qui a Deo infinite superantur. Hinc Nazianzenus, Platonem corrigens: Dei naturam nullis verbis explicari posse, animo atque intellectu comprehendi multo minus posse.
